meta.description: Per GPU: median leave-one-GPU-out residual of three models across SPEC GWPG disclosures (SPECviewperf, SPECworkstation, SPECapc), predicted calibrated scores with 80% ranges, evidence counts and spread across submitted configurations.

sources.name: SPEC Graphics and Workstation Performance Group (GWPG) published results
sources.licence: SPEC Fair Use Rules (https://www.spec.org/products/fairuse). Public use is allowed when the source and retrieval date are stated, the licensee of each result is identifiable, the SPEC, SPECviewperf, SPECworkstation and SPECapc trademarks are acknowledged, SPEC metrics are compared only within the same benchmark release and resolution, and derived values and estimates are clearly labelled and never called SPEC metrics. The site does all of these.
sources.frequency: weekly collection; SPEC/GWPG publishes new workstation and GPU results periodically
sources.typical_lag: results appear weeks to months after the test date

limitations: SPEC GWPG results (SPECviewperf 15/2020/13/12.1, SPECworkstation 4.0/3.1/3.0, and SPECapc Maya/Solidworks/Creo/3ds Max) are submitted by workstation OEMs (Dell, HP, Lenovo, Fujitsu, MIFCOM) and GPU vendors.

Because SPEC GWPG spans multiple benchmark generations, OS families and resolutions, each suite-OS-resolution cohort is calibrated onto the SPECviewperf 2020 v3 Windows FHD/QHD scale against physical hardware throughput, refitted inside every leave-one-GPU-out fold. Only cohorts that pass the held-out calibration check (gpu_calibration) feed the ranking.
Predicted scores and residuals are this site's estimates derived from SPEC GWPG disclosures. They are not official SPEC metrics.
SPEC, SPECviewperf, SPECworkstation, and SPECapc are trademarks or registered trademarks of the Standard Performance Evaluation Corporation. Every row links to its official SPEC disclosure.
meta.spec_source: Shader count, clock, VRAM and bandwidth come from a specification table maintained in this repository (pdi/tech_value/gwpg.py), not from SPEC.

finding.label: explanation
finding.reason: A GPU residual is the part of a graphics card's calibrated SPEC GWPG score its shader count, boost clock, VRAM capacity and memory bandwidth do not account for. It flags cards to look at more closely; it does not say why.
